This is an appeal under Section 374(3)(A) Cr.P.C. challenging the judgment of conviction dated 17.10.2022 and order on the point of sentence dated 20.10.2022 passed by Ms. Nabeela Wali, Ld. Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Kiran by Kiran Gupta Gupta 15:15:51 +0530 New Delhi. Kiran by Kiran Gupta Gupta 15:16:19
texts.facts: The Ld. ACCM vide impugned judgment dated 17.10.2022 had convicted the appellant for violation of offence punishable under Section 2(ia) r/w Rule 44(c) r/w S. 7 of PFA punishable under S. 16(1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration (hereinafter referred as PFA) Act and violation of S. 14A of the Act punishable under S. 16(1)(c) of the Act. a. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the respondent has not complied with mandatory procedures and rules under the Act. b. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that appellants right to seek second opinion from CFL under S. 13(2) of PFA was violated by the respondent as no PA report was ever received by the appellant. The respondent further failed to prove that the appellant was duly served with the PA report via post. That the Trial Court failed to appreciate that there was inordinate delay in instituting prosecution in the present case. The PA report was received on 06.07.2009 by the respondent and prosecution was instituted much lateron 23.11.2009. d. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that no independent witness was joined by the respondent while purchasing samples. e. That the Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate the material contradiction in the testimony of witnesses examined by the respondent.
texts.arguments: Though the appellant has taken the said ground, however, he has nowhere described as to how and in which manner the deposition of witnesses were against the facts or contrary to each other.

14. In view of above, question for consideration before this court is whether after repeal of earlier Act and introduction of new Act which contains the lesser punishment, the court can take a lenient view of awarding the lesser punishment.

15. The recent judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr.
(Supra) has made it clear that if there is an amendment in the Act, which is beneficial to the accused,
